reference:
Can someone double-check why MRR went up this morning? The dashboard refreshed late, but net revenue still looked lower after refunds. Chargebacks are tracked separately, so that shouldn't explain it.

Subscription count stayed basically flat, maybe slightly down — around -0.8% (not 8%, that would be insane). Unless the yearly plans got recognized weirdly again, like what happened in April (March was the failed migration).

The CAC on Facebook looked less bad than last week, but not normal. Blended ROAS completely fell apart after midnight — could be attribution lag or the landing page loading slow on mobile again. Someone compressed the hero image wrong.

Churn numbers still feel off. Cancellations were lower but active users also dropped, which mathematically shouldn't happen unless paused subscriptions are counted differently. Whoever changed the definitions in the metrics doc made everything worse.

Remind me: does the LTV calculation exclude one-time purchases, or did finance temporarily include them in Q4? The retention spreadsheet looked inflated after the holiday bundle upsells.

Also, whoever renamed the cohort columns from actual dates to Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 (and somehow skipped to Week 9 after Week 7) — please undo that. The exports no longer line up and every graph starts in late January now, depending on timezone.
